the tetrameric G3PDH has a D2-symmetrical conformation, with two active and two inactive sites in the tetrameric molecule.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GPDH molecule is in D2-symmetrical conformation at pH 7 and C2-symmetrical at pH 8.6.
the D2-symmetric conformation is a kinetic artifact, and that the enzyme exists in the C2-symmetric form under normal physiological conditions.
the tetrameric GpDH from mung beans exists predominantly in the C2-symmetrical conformation with the four SH groups in the active sites being equivalent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inactivation kinetics with these SH-reagents can provide information about the quaternary structure of the enzyme.
the conformational state of GPDH in solution is not the same as the one observed in the crystal structure and that it can exist in two distinct conformational states.
the inactivation of a protein with an SH reagent does not necessarily provide information on the number of reactive SH groups.
